issues.legal_issue: A deceased coparcener’s interest that devolves by intestate succession to Class I heirs is inherited individually by those heirs rather than as joint family property.
material_facts: A coparcener died intestate, leaving a wife and daughters who were Class I heirs.
A notional partition immediately before his death would have determined his share in the coparcenary property.
The deceased’s share was claimed by his heirs in a suit for partition.
issues.conclusion: The deceased’s share devolved under the Hindu Succession Act to his heirs individually, who held it as tenants in common; it did not remain joint family property.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 6 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, including its proviso and Explanation 1, where a male Hindu leaves a Class I female heir, his coparcenary interest devolves by succession, with that interest determined by a notional partition immediately before death. Sections 8 and 19 provide for succession to heirs per capita as tenants in common, and Section 30 treats a coparcener’s interest as disposable property. Section 4(b) displaces inconsistent prior Hindu law. Gurupad Khandappa Magdum v. Hirabai Khandappa Magdum explains that the consequences of the deemed partition must be worked out; Commissioner of Wealth Tax v. Chander Sen and Appropriate Authority (IT Deptt) v. M. Arifulla establish that property devolving under Section 8 is individual property held by heirs as tenants in common, not HUF property.

predicates.partition_claim_over_intestate_coparcena: The proceeding seeks partition of an interest in coparcenary property after its holder died intestate.
predicates.deceased_left_class_one_female_heirs: The deceased left one or more female heirs who qualify as Class I heirs.

issues.definition: When a partition claim concerns an intestate coparcener’s property and the deceased left Class I female heirs, the inherited interest is individual property held in common by the heirs.

issues.legal_issue: A mother may act as the natural guardian of a minor whose share is relinquished in a family settlement, and the resulting disposition is voidable rather than void when the required court permission was not obtained.
material_facts: A mother executed a registered release on behalf of her minor daughter, relinquishing the daughter’s share in favour of other family members.
The release formed part of an arrangement dissolving or settling the family’s interests in the property.
The Karta was among the persons in whose favour the minor’s share was relinquished, creating a conflict if the Karta were treated as the minor’s guardian.
No court permission was obtained for the disposition.
issues.conclusion: The mother, not the Karta, could act as the minor’s natural guardian in the circumstances; the release was not void ab initio but was at most voidable.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 6 and 8 of the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956 govern natural guardianship and a natural guardian’s powers. Section 6 excludes a minor’s undivided interest in joint family property from its general rule, but a Karta is the manager of the joint family, not the guardian of its minor members. Where a family settlement relinquishes a minor’s share in favour of the Karta, the conflict prevents the Karta from acting for the minor; the mother is the natural guardian. Under Section 8, a disposition of a minor’s immovable property without the required prior court permission is voidable at the minor’s instance, not void.

rule.if: minor_property_release_dispute and mother_executed_release_for_minor and minor_share_relinquished_in_family_settlement and no_court_permission_was_obtained

predicates.minor_property_release_dispute: The proceeding concerns a disposition of property belonging to a minor.
predicates.mother_executed_release_for_minor: The minor’s mother executed a release on the minor’s behalf.
predicates.minor_share_relinquished_in_family_settl: The minor’s share was relinquished as part of a family settlement in favour of another family member.
predicates.no_court_permission_was_obtained: The required prior court permission for the disposition was not obtained.

issues.definition: When a mother executes a release for a minor as part of a family settlement without the required court permission, the release is voidable rather than void.

issues.legal_issue: A minor’s challenge to a voidable disposition of immovable property is time-barred when it is brought after the applicable limitation period following the minor’s attainment of majority.
material_facts: The plaintiff was a minor when her mother executed the release on her behalf.
The plaintiff attained majority but did not challenge the release within three years thereafter.
The partition suit was filed later, seeking to claim the share covered by the release.
issues.conclusion: The release could not be challenged as void after the applicable limitation period had expired; the trial court’s dismissal of the suit was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Section 8(3) of the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956 makes a disposition in contravention of the applicable requirements voidable at the instance of the minor or a person claiming under the minor. The Court held that the plaintiff should have challenged the release within three years of attaining majority; the trial court’s dismissal on limitation was therefore restored.

predicates.partition_suit_challenging_minor_release: The proceeding seeks partition based on a claim that a release executed for a minor does not bind the minor.
predicates.minor_did_not_challenge_release_within_a: The minor attained majority and did not challenge the release within the applicable limitation period thereafter.

issues.definition: When a partition suit challenges a release executed for a minor, but the minor did not challenge it within the applicable period after attaining majority, the late challenge cannot set the release aside.
